performance.cable-capacity-basis: ESTIMATE, not stated by FS - Cat6 24AWG (6.1 mm). A channel cross-section of 62.9 x 149.6 mm (9409.8 mm2) at 4.7 mm2 a cable, the figure FS's own Cat6 counts for the CMV-SFD45U5W and CMV-DFD45U5W imply, rounded down. That is FS's scale, not a packing: 4.7 mm2 is a sixth of one cable's section. The width rests on estimated walls (see provenance `capacity`)

attrs.note: datasheet - style, colour, the included brackets and fixings, the open racks it matches and RoHS and ISO 9001 are the specification table and Standards Compliance list of the datasheet and the product page; the materials are under `material`.

bottom.note: drawing - the bottom end is the top end again: the side view is the same at both ends.

capacity.note: estimated - FS states no cable capacity for CMV-SFD42U9W: the cable capacity table of its datasheet lists CMV-5U3W, CMV-SFD45U5W and CMV-DFD45U5W and not this part, and the product page gives none. So the 2002 is worked out, not read. METHOD: the channel's inside cross-section, the `duct` guide width by the depth from the front face of the web to the rear face of the cover plate on the side view of the 42U vertical datasheet, divided by 4.7 mm2 a Cat6 cable. 4.7 is the mm2 a cable that FS's own Cat6 counts imply for CMV-SFD45U5W (12767.8 mm2 for 2745, 4.65) and CMV-DFD45U5W (two channels, 25535.6 mm2 for 5490, 4.65), rounded up to 0.1; the count is rounded down. The CMV-5U3W is not used: an open bracket with no cover has no closed channel (it implies 5.2). CROSS-SECTION: 62.9 x 149.6 = 9409.8 mm2, and 9409.8 / 4.7 = 2002.1. THE FIGURE IS FS'S SCALE, NOT A PACKING: 4.65 mm2 is a sixth of the 29.2 mm2 section of one 6.1 mm cable, so FS's vertical counts are not a fill of the channel, and this one is as far from one. It puts this part beside its sisters on the same table. The 62.9 width rests on the walls this file estimates at 13 (provenance `guides`): 10 or 16 would move the count by about 10 per cent. The depth is taken from the 1.5 mm web, the floor of this channel, to the cover plate; the 45U calibration parts start at a solid 26.9 mm back plate, and measuring from this part's 37.2 mm channel flanges instead would give 106.2 mm deep and a count of 1421. The count is of Cat6 24AWG and is marked as an estimate (`cable-capacity-estimated`).

chassis.note: datasheet - THE DUCT AS IT STANDS, cover fitted: `width` across the rack face direction, `height` the height it runs, `depth` front to back. 1866.9 x 88.9 x 152.6 is the specification table (73.5 x 3.5 x 6.00 in), and 1866.9 is 42 x 44.45. The side view prints 152.6 from the back of the channel to the front of the cover; the render x1 dimensions 3.5 in across the cover and 6.00 in along the side, and a section 36.75 in [933mm].

color.note: estimated - "Color: Black". Every image FS publishes of the part is a render; it is drawn in the shades of the FS ABS ducts, the cover a shade lighter.

cover.note: drawing - THE SOURCES DISAGREE AND THE DRAWING IS TAKEN. The product page style is Finger Duct, with no cover, and the specification table lists none; the drawing has a Cover Back View, the render x1 shows the cover closed and swung open, and renders g2, g3 and g6 to g8 show it fitted. The cover is drawn, one a section, and the disagreement is a `gaps:` entry.

fingers-shape.note: drawing - the side view draws each finger as a T: a V widening to its root at the wall, a stem 12.7 high, and a crossbar along the duct at its front end; renders g6, g8 and x4 show the same T, moulded, clipped into square windows along the channel flange. The V is drawn as a block, and the crossbar is estimated at 30 high.

floor.note: estimated - the floor of the well is the front of the web, taken 1.5 from the rear: the side view draws the web at the back of the 152.6 as a single line.

front.note: drawing - the covers, fitted. With them off the front is the channel between the two finger walls, the crossbars of the fingers end-on along each edge and the web with its windows and keyholes at the bottom of it. The walls are taken 13 wide (the back view draws a strip of small square windows down each edge about that wide), so the channel is 62.9. The 42 fingers stand at one rack unit, centred in each section.

guides.note: estimated - the duct on the front view is the channel between the two finger walls, 62.9 wide on the estimated 13 walls, run down the height (`run: y`); its finger pitch is the rack unit of the side view and its gap the 31.75 between stems.

left.note: drawing - the side view of the datasheet, rear at x=0: the channel flange, the row of finger bases, 42 fingers and the edge of the two covers, with the joint a seam. The bracket plates the view hangs behind the channel are not drawn.

material.note: drawing - THE SOURCES DISAGREE AND THE RENDERS ARE TAKEN. The product page gives the body material as SPCC; the datasheet gives the backbone as Plastic (ABS), and both the datasheet heading and the page title call it a plastic manager. The renders g4, g5 and g7 show a folded sheet channel with punched square holes, countersunk screws and sheared edges, and moulded T fingers clipped into it, so the backbone is stated as SPCC and the fingers as plastic. The disagreement is a `gaps:` entry.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE VENDOR DRAWING, AT THE RESOLUTION IT HAS. The FS 42U Vertical Cable Managers with Finger Ducts datasheet (page 5) draws the whole duct three ways - a back view, a side view and a cover back view - in millimetres, and notes that it is two equal parts, 73.5 in (1866.9mm) high. The embedded rasters are about 100 by 720 px, so every figure is read on the 600 dpi page render, where each native pixel is a 5 px block, and only as a fraction of a figure the same view prints: the side view 152.6 across (283 px) and 1866.9 down (3090 px), the back view its 311, 1555 and 228.2 down and the stated 88.9 across. The two axes of one view differ by up to 10 per cent, so nothing is carried between axes. The product-page renders of #188944 are the second reading (x1 dimensioned, cover closed and open; g2 straight on; g4, g5, g7 the channel; g6 and g8 the fingers and the cover hinge; g9 the included brackets and fixings).

mount.note: drawing - `rack-side`. The side view hangs four brackets off the back of the duct, 622, 311 and 622 apart, and FS compatibility matrix accepts the part on the APC AR201 45U two-post and the AR203A 44U four-post open frames; the specification table says it matches 42U and 45U open racks. No install guide is published for it. The brackets (Quick Release Brackets x4 and Brackets x4, render g9 and x2) are hardware and are not drawn. It occupies no rack unit; `ru: 42` is the height it runs beside, and which side of the rack is a lab placement to say (docs/vertical-cable-managers-design.md).

rear.note: drawing - the back view: the web 88.9 wide with six rectangular windows on its centre line, 47.3 wide and 146.4 high, each a declared pass-through, open, through into the channel; a keyhole above each (R11 over R6.78), the first 83.7 below the top and 311 apart, and a small window 26.8 by 31.6 below each of the first five large ones, painted. The view is symmetric about its centre line, so the rear is the back view unmirrored.

rear-not-drawn.note: drawing - the rows of small square windows down both edges of the web, the screw holes and the brackets are not drawn: the windows are the clips of the finger bases seen through the web, under one native pixel each, and the brackets are hardware.

right.note: drawing - the left view mirrored: the duct is the same on both sides.

sections.note: drawing - THE TWO SECTIONS ARE DRAWN AS ONE LENGTH, each 933.45, half the 1866.9, with the joint a seam. The cover back view draws the two covers meeting at the joint, and the render x1 dimensions a section 933 mm.

shell.note: drawing - A HOLLOW DUCT, NOT A BOX, as every FS finger duct in the library is (docs/cable-managers-design.md section 4). The body is a sheet body and its six views are elevations; the solid is what its parts build: the web of the channel as a well 151.1 deep on the front view, its floor open at the six windows; the two finger walls and 84 fingers standing in it; and the two covers, which pull off and open the channel. The back is built as plates sunk 0.05 inside the rear face, round the windows.

thickness.note: estimated - no FS document states a gauge. 1.5 is the web and the cover plate; the parts carry their own thicknesses.

top.note: drawing - the end of the duct seen from above, rear at y=0, from the side view depths: the web, the channel flanges to 37.2, the finger bases to 65.2, the V root, stem and crossbar to 143.4, the cover lips and the cover plate to 152.6. No view draws the end; it is the side view figures laid across the back view widths.
